title: Round 6 / ECDLP-18: decisive genus-2 cover index-calculus test
question: For E/F_p and a genus-2 cover C -> E (e.g. the double cover w^2 = x(Q) - c), does index calculus in J_C(F_p) with a degree-1 factor base solve DLPs in pi^*(E(F_p)) at a measured cost below sqrt(p) at toy sizes (p up to ~2^16), or does it cost >= q as predicted by HYP-ad5bc0e3?
claims: Experimental (toy domain, p<=2^14): Gaudry-style degree-1 factor-base index calculus on J_C(F_p) for the genus-2 double cover y^2=f(w^2+c) of prime-order E recovered the DL (equal to BSGS and the secret) on 12/12 curves; median counted cost 99,866 / 3.78e6 / 1.17e8 / 3.85e9 at p=251/1021/4093/16381 (Cantor-only 292/1,024/4,162/16,410, ~p; log-log slope 0.97, total slope 2.52), versus sqrt(p)=15.8..128. HYP-ad5bc0e3 prediction (cost >= ~p) SURVIVES the pre-registered falsification rule; not falsified.

No imaginary (degree-5) model exists for any double cover of E with #E odd prime: Weierstrass points lie over E[2]\{O}; the degree-6 model with infty+/infty- was used. Group law verified (associativity, hom pi^*, [#J]D=0, L-poly #J=r*#E' on all curves run).

Pullback-only relations (Variant A) have disjoint supports (confirmed: dedup relations never determine k, rank ~ half the unknowns); raw A recovers k only by a birthday collision in E (first collision ~0.9 sqrt(r) trials), not by the cover.
Reduced-factor-base variant (half base) doubled Cantor cost (p/f model); large-prime/GTTD variants not implemented (analytic only). Experiments do not establish asymptotics.
next_action: Independent review of hyper2.py and Variant A collision analysis; optionally 2^16 with Wiedemann LA and a GTTD large-prime variant; PI to decide whether to update HYP-ad5bc0e3 evidence/notes (not edited by this run).
